units.text: I wrote a Python program that used pandas groupby on customer_id to aggregate purchase amounts into one total per customer.
I checked the program's totals against hand-calculated totals for two customers and confirmed that a customer with no purchases produced zero.

rationale: Explicit personal Python implementation, a specific groupby operation, and an executed check with expected outputs and a boundary case. Numerical improvement is unnecessary.

units.text: I personally used pandas in Python for a customer-data preparation task. I planned to check the resulting data later.

rationale: Explicit personal use of a Python library for a stated task satisfies core practice. No concrete operation, procedure, or integration detail is described. A planned check is not an executed check. Under the proposed binary c2 rule, a library name is not partial credit.

units.text: Technical skills: Python, pandas, NumPy, PyTorch.

rationale: A bare skills list is knowledge/listing evidence and does not establish the personal practice required by these three criteria. This is not a claim that the applicant lacks the skill.

units.text: Our team built and tested a Python invoice parser that converted PDFs into rows. I participated in the project as a research assistant.

rationale: Relevant Python implementation exists, but the applicant's own programming contribution is unresolved. The proposed core-first rule leaves the skill pending and does not borrow the team's method or testing as personal c2/c3 evidence.

units.text: I implemented and tested a video pipeline using OpenCV's C++ API. This implementation contained no Python code or Python library calls.

rationale: The source explicitly identifies a C++ implementation and rules out Python. A library also having Python bindings cannot override that evidence.

units.text: I wrote a Python CSV-cleaning function that removed rows with empty customer_id values. I tested this function.

rationale: The source states an actual personal test of the same function, but supplies no test case, observed behavior, diagnostic finding, or expected-output comparison. This is the deliberately narrow c3 partial category.

units.text: I fine-tuned Qwen3-VL, a vision-language model, to transcribe photographed handwritten labels into text. I supplied image-and-instruction pairs and decoded model responses into text labels.
I compared the model's transcriptions against reference transcriptions for held-out label images and inspected character substitution errors.

rationale: A named vision-language model is explicitly used for a language task with textual output, so its image input does not disqualify it. Input/output details and an executed reference-based check are stated.

units.text: I used GPT-4.1 to summarize meeting transcripts, sending each transcript with an instruction to return three bullet points. I built an output-saving workflow for future evaluation of the summaries.

rationale: Named language-model use and a concrete input/output configuration establish c1/c2. Building a workflow for future evaluation does not state that any output was checked.

units.text: Skills: large language models, GPT, Qwen, prompt engineering.

rationale: The list names relevant technologies but establishes neither a personal language-model task nor a performed check.

units.text: Our team used GPT-4.1 to turn customer notes into short summaries and reviewed the outputs for omitted facts. I supported the project as a student assistant.

rationale: The team's language-model use is clear, but the applicant's contribution could be unrelated support. Core ownership remains unresolved; the team result cannot establish the applicant's c2/c3.

units.text: I trained a ResNet image classifier to assign defect categories and evaluated its class accuracy. The project did not use a language model or generate text.

rationale: A neural image classifier and its evaluation do not establish a language-model task; the source explicitly excludes one.

units.text: I used GPT-4.1 with a system instruction to turn each support ticket into a two-sentence summary. I checked the generated summaries.

rationale: Personal model use and an input/output configuration are explicit. Checking the same outputs was performed, but no requirement, example, error category, or observed comparison is supplied.

units.text: I implemented an assistant in which a language model requested a lookup_order tool call with an order_id. My program required human approval before executing that request and passed the returned order status back to the model.
I tested a rejected approval and verified that lookup_order was not executed, and tested an approved request against the expected order status.

rationale: Explicit personal implementation, model-requested tool invocation, a concrete argument/result and human approval path, and executed control/tool-result checks. One tool and human review remain eligible.

units.text: I implemented a workflow where a language model emitted a search_catalog call, my code executed the call using the model's query argument, and the returned product IDs were appended to the model context. I prepared a test harness for later checks of failed tool calls.

rationale: The model-mediated invocation and result-handling workflow is explicit. Preparing a harness for future checks does not establish that any tool failure or result was actually checked.

units.text: Skills: AI agents, LangChain, function calling, tool use.

rationale: Technology names alone establish no personally designed or implemented model-mediated tool/action workflow.

units.text: I built an explainable decision agent that combined OCR outputs, engineering rules, and retrieved documents to produce traceable interpretations and route difficult cases for review.

rationale: Personal implementation and an agent label are present, but whether a model mediates the tool/action workflow remains unresolved. OCR, rules, retrieval and review routing alone neither prove nor expressly rule out that identity.

units.text: I built and tested a decision agent whose routing used only fixed if-else rules and keyword search. No language model or other learned model participated in its decisions, tool requests, or action control.

rationale: The source explicitly excludes model mediation. Its agent label and software tests cannot substitute for the required workflow identity.

units.text: I implemented a language-model assistant that requested get_weather with a city argument; my code invoked the tool and returned its temperature value to the model. I tested this tool-handling workflow.

rationale: Personal implementation, model mediation, a concrete invocation and returned value are explicit. Testing the same workflow occurred, but the checked behavior, error case or expected result is not stated.

units.text: I used Python and pandas for data preparation in an insurance-claims project. I have not yet checked that work.

rationale: The applicant explicitly performed a stated task using Python and pandas, satisfying c1. Data preparation names a task category, but no actual operation, transformation, function, library procedure, or input/output connection is described. The source expressly says the work has not been checked.

units.text: I used Python and pandas in an insurance-claims project to remove rows with missing policy_id values before producing a cleaned claims table. I have not yet checked that work.

rationale: This pairs with x001 but adds a concrete row-removal operation and its condition. That detail satisfies c2 without source code, an exact API name, or reproducibility requirements. The explicit absence of checking keeps c3 not_evidenced.

units.text: I personally used NumPy in Python for data processing in a laboratory-measurement project. No validation of that work was performed.

rationale: Personal use of a Python library for a stated task establishes c1. Data processing and the laboratory application domain do not specify what operation or transformation was performed, so c2 receives no detail credit. Validation is explicitly absent.

units.text: I personally used NumPy in Python to reshape each flat sequence of 24 laboratory measurements into a 4-by-6 array.
I checked the reshaped array against a hand-arranged example and verified that the original measurement order was preserved.

rationale: This pairs with x003 but states an actual reshape operation and its input/output structure. A separate unit states an executed check of the same operation against a concrete example and order-preservation criterion, supporting c3.
